newsitem.title: MEXICO: States battle for second Mexico City airport site.
newsitem.headline: States battle for second Mexico City airport site.

text.p: Two Mexican states are battling to convince the federal government to locate a new, second airport for Mexico City in towns surrounding the capital.
The choice lies between a long-term costly option and a short-term solution that could wreck a man-made wildlife reserve, analysts say.
Regardless of the decision, observers say the decision should come soon as the flood of visitors to the capital, home to some 20 million people, is testing existing facilities.
The Hidalgo state proposal would build four new runways at the site of Tizayuca, about 60 km north of the capital.
But the town's location would require costly infrastructure development, said an airline analyst who asked not to be named.

Closer to the nation's capital, 20 km away, is the proposed airport site at Texcoco in the State of Mexico. However, construction there would ruin the man-made ecological reserve between the capital and the industrial town, the analyst said.

Also, the Texcoco site only has space for two runways that would likely fill growing traffic needs for only 20 years, he said, while the expanded Tizayuca site could contain passenger growth for about 40 years.
Hidalgo government officials say they plan to spend $20 billion if granted the project, and draw foreign companies to build a planned industrial park in the area.
Eugenio Imaz, the state's minister for trade and industry, said Mexican construction firms Empresas ICA and Grupo Tribasa have expressed interest in the project.

Officials in the State of Mexico say though that the western part of the state being considered for the new airport is a better option because it already has some infrastructure as well as a client base of foreign companies and a larger population.
"All things being equal, we are the biggest population center in the country," said Juan Jose Guerra Abud, economic development secretary for the state of Mexico.
